pages.text: The sun had blazed for days. Garden soil dried pale, and thirsty pea shoots drooped.
Nils wanted to water them himself. "I'll do the watering!" He lifted the watering can.
He filled it from the water tub beside the well. The can was heavy.
Nils ran to the garden. Slosh, slosh! Water spilled out, leaving dots along the path.
At the garden, the can was light. He tipped it. A trickle, just a few drops.
Water marks covered the path from well to garden. Nils panted, out of breath.
But the garden soil was still pale and dry. Nils dropped to the ground.
Grandpa pointed at the water marks. "Can you get there without making these?"
This time, the can was only half full. Nils walked slowly, one step at a time. No sloshing.
Pour, pour. Every shoot had a good drink. Wet soil smelled lovely. The shoots looked bright again.
